context.title: Volunteers for the Holy City
context.summary: The leaders settle in Jerusalem, and lots are cast so one family in ten will move there; others volunteer. The chapter lists Jerusalem's residents and the towns of Judah and Benjamin where others lived.
context.background: Living in Jerusalem meant leaving farmland and facing danger, so those who volunteered were publicly blessed (v. 2). A full list of residents parallels 1 Chronicles 9. Settlements stretched from Beersheba in the south to the Valley of Hinnom (v. 30).

customs.note: Drawing lots chose one household in ten — a kind of tithe of the people for the city.

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Pharez
people.summary: Pharez,, breach, the son of Judah (Neh. 11:4). “The chief of all the captains of the host for the first month” in the reign of David was taken from his family (1 Chr. 27:3).

people.name: Shephatiah
people.summary: Descendant of Perez, of the tribe of Judah, whose great-great-grandson was chosen by lot to dwell in Jerusalem when Nehemiah rebuilt the city.

people.name: Jesaiah
people.summary: Son of Hananiah; tribe of Judah.

people.name: Jedaiah
people.summary: A priest in Jerusalem after the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

people.name: Joiarib
people.summary: The founder of one of the courses of the priests (Neh. 11:10).

people.name: Jachin
people.summary: One of the priests who returned from the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

people.name: Hilkiah
people.summary: The high priest in the reign of Josiah (1 Chr. 6:13; Ezra 7:1). To him and his deputy (2 Kings 23:5), along with the ordinary priests and the Levites who had charge of the gates, was entrusted the purification of the temple in Jerusalem.

people.name: Meraioth
people.summary: Father of Amariah, a high priest of the line of Eleazar (1 Chr. 6:6, 7, 52).

people.name: Jeroham
people.summary: 1 Chr. 9:12; a priest, perhaps the same as in Neh. 11:12.

people.name: Malchijah
people.summary: The first Malchijah mentioned in the Bible was a priest of ancient Israel after the order of Aaron, during the reign of King David in the 10th century BC. Malchijah led the fifth of the 24 priestly divisions. The biblical passage of 1 Chronicles 24 documents the division of the priests during the reign of King David. These priests were all descendants of Aaron, who had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. However, Nadab and Abihu died before Aaron and only Eleazar and Ithamar had sons. One priest, Zadok, from Eleazar's descendants and another priest, Ahimelech, from Ithamar's descendants were designated to help create the various priestly orders. Sixteen of Eleazar's descendants were selected to head priestly orders while only eight of Ithamar's descendants were so chosen. The passage states that this was done because of the greater number of leaders among Eleazar's descendants. Lots were drawn to designate the order of ministering for the heads of the priestly orders when they entered the temple. Since each order was responsible for ministering during a different week, Malchijah's order was stationed as a watch at the Tabernacle during the fifth week of the year on the Hebrew calendar.

people.name: Maasiai
people.summary: Work of Jehovah, one of the priests resident at Jerusalem at the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:12).

people.name: Meshillemith
people.summary: A priest, the son of Immer (Neh. 11:13).

people.name: Zabdiel
people.summary: An overseer of the priests after the Captivity (Neh. 11:14).

people.name: Hashabiah
people.summary: One of the Levite leaders in the time of Ezra.

people.name: Hasshub
people.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (Neh. 11:15; 1 Chr. 9:14).

people.name: Obadiah
people.summary: A Levite, after the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:16).

people.name: Micha
people.summary: The son of Zabdi, a Levite of the family of Asaph (Neh. 11:17, 22).

people.name: Zichri
people.summary: A Levite, one of the sons of Asaph (Neh. 11:17); probably the same as Zichri (1 Chr. 9:15), and Zaccur (Neh. 12:35).

people.name: Akkub
people.summary: A Levite who kept the gate of the temple after the return from Babylon (1 Chr. 9:17; Ezra 2:42; Neh. 7:45).

people.name: Asaph
people.summary: A Levite; one of the leaders of David’s choir (1 Chr. 6:39). Psalms 50 and 73-83 inclusive are attributed to him. He is mentioned along with David as skilled in music, and a “seer” (2 Chr. 29:30).

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: A son of Tamar (Gen. 38:30); called also Zara (Matt. 1:3).

people.name: Pethahiah
people.summary: A descendant of Judah who had some office at the court of Persia (Neh. 11:24).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Ophel
places.summary: Hill; mound, the long, narrow, rounded promontory on the southern slope of the temple hill, between the Tyropoeon and the Kedron valley (2 Chr. 27:3; 33:14; Neh. 3:26, 27).

places.name: Dibon
places.summary: A city of the tribe of Judah, inhabited after the Captivity (Neh. 11:25); called also Dimonah (Josh. 15:22).

places.name: Jeshua
places.summary: A city of Judah (Neh. 11:26).

places.name: Moladah
places.summary: Birth, a city in the south of Judah which fell to Simeon (Josh. 15:21-26; 19:2).

places.name: Beersheba
places.summary: Well of the oath, or well of seven, a well dug by Abraham, and so named because he and Abimelech here entered into a compact (Gen. 21:31). On re-opening it, Isaac gave it the same name (Gen. 26:31-33).

places.name: Hazar-shual
places.summary: Village or enclosure of the jackal, a city on the south border of Judah (Josh. 15:28; Neh. 11:27).

places.name: Meconah
places.summary: A base or foundation, a town in the south of Judah (Neh. 11:28), near Ziklag.

places.name: Ziklag
places.summary: A town in the Negeb, or south country of Judah (Josh. 15:31), in the possession of the Philistines when David fled to Gath from Ziph with all his followers.

places.name: Jarmuth
places.summary: A town in the plain of Judah (Josh. 15:35), originally the residence of one of the Canaanitish kings (10:3, 5, 23).

places.name: Adullam
places.summary: One of the royal cities of the Canaanites, now ‘Aid-el-ma (Josh. 12:15; 15:35). It stood on the old Roman road in the valley of Elah, which was the scene of David’s memorable victory over Goliath (1 Sam. 17:2), and not far from Gath.

places.name: Azekah
places.summary: Dug over, a town in the Shephelah or low hills of Judah (Josh. 15:35), where the five confederated Amoritish kings were defeated by Joshua and their army destroyed by a hailstrom (10:10, 11).

places.name: Lachish
places.summary: Impregnable, a royal Canaanitish city in the Shephelah, or maritime plain of Palestine (Josh. 10:3, 5; 12:11). It was taken and destroyed by the Israelites (Josh. 10:31-33).

places.name: valley of Hinnom
places.summary: A deep, narrow ravine separating Mount Zion from the so-called “Hill of Evil Counsel.” It took its name from “some ancient hero, the son of Hinnom.”

places.name: Zanoah
places.summary: A town in the low country or shephelah of Judah, near Zorah (Josh. 15:34). It was re-occupied after the return from the Captivity (Neh. 11:30).

places.name: Bethel
places.summary: A place in Central Palestine, about 10 miles north of Jerusalem, at the head of the pass of Michmash and Ai. It was originally the royal Canaanite city of Luz (Gen. 28:19).

places.name: Geba
places.summary: The hill, (2 Sam. 5:25 [1 Chr. 14:16, “Gibeon”]; 2 Kings 23:8; Neh. 11:31), a Levitical city of Benjamin (1 Kings 15:22; 1 Sam. 13:16; 14:5, wrongly “Gibeah” in the A.V.), on the north border of Judah near Gibeah (Isa. 10:29; Josh. 18:24, 28).

places.name: Michmash
places.summary: Something hidden, a town of Benjamin (Ezra 2:27), east of Bethel and south of Migron, on the road to Jerusalem (Isa. 10:28). It lay on the line of march of an invading army from the north, on the north side of the steep and precipitous Wady es-Suweinit (“valley of the little thorn-tree” or “the acacia”), and now bears the name of Mukhmas.

places.name: Ananiah
places.summary: Protected by Jehovah, the name of a town in the tribe of Benjamin between Nob and Hazor (Neh. 11:32).

places.name: Anathoth
places.summary: The name of one of the cities of refuge, in the tribe of Benjamin (Josh. 21:18). The Jews, as a rule, did not change the names of the towns they found in Palestine; hence this town may be regarded as deriving its name from the goddess Anat.

places.name: Nob
places.summary: High place, a city of the priests, first mentioned in the history of David’s wanderings (1 Sam. 21:1). Here the tabernacle was then standing, and here Ahimelech the priest resided.

places.name: Gittaim
places.summary: Two wine-presses, (2 Sam. 4:3; Neh. 11:33), a town probably in Benjamin to which the Beerothites fled.

places.name: Ramah
places.summary: A city first mentioned in Josh. 18:25, near Gibeah of Benjamin. It was fortified by Baasha, king of Israel (1 Kings 15:17-22; 2 Chr. 16:1-6).

places.name: Hadid
places.summary: Pointed, a place in the tribe of Benjamin near Lydda, or Lod, and Ono (Ezra 2:33; Neh. 7:37).

places.name: Neballat
places.summary: Wickedness in secret, (Neh. 11:34), probably the village of Beit Nebala, about 4 miles north of Lydda.

places.name: Zeboim
places.summary: A place mentioned only in Neh. 11:34, inhabited by the Benjamites after the Captivity.

places.name: Ono
places.summary: A town of Benjamin, in the “plain of Ono” (1 Chr. 8:12; Ezra 2:33); now Kefr ‘Ana, 5 miles north of Lydda, and about 30 miles north-west of Jerusalem.
